newsitem.title: FRANCE: Algerian courts condemn 14 Islamists to death.
newsitem.headline: Algerian courts condemn 14 Islamists to death.

text.p: Algerian courts have condemned to death 14 Moslem fundamentalists, most of them on the run, the official Algerian news agency APS said on Sunday.
A court sitting in Medea, 60 km (40 miles) southwest of Algiers sentenced eight fugitives to death on Saturday for belonging to "an armed terrorist group aiming to spread death".

In Bechar, a town some 760 km (470 miles) southwest of the capital, the court condemned six people to death for "terrorist affairs", APS said. Three of the accused stood trial in the court while the other three were tried in their absence.

Earlier this month, APS said Medea court had sentenced 23 Islamists to death, also in their absence. They were accused of crimes including "belonging to an armed movement, undermining state security, taking part in premeditated murder, sabotage and arson of economic units and educational establishments."

Algerian authorities have been locked in conflict with Moslem fundamentalists since early 1992. Violence started in the North African country shortly after the authorities cancelled a general election in which Islamists had swept to a commanding lead in the first round.
